name: Create
comment: The `Create` class helps you create structures from sets of points.

signatures.comment: Create a Delaunay Group. Use the [`Delaunay.delaunay()`](#link) and [`Delaunay.voronoi()`](#link) functions in the returned group to generate tessellations.
signatures.returns_comment: an instance of the Delaunay class

parameters.name: pts
parameters.comment: a Group or an array of Pts

signatures.comment: Create a set of points that distribute evenly on a line. Similar to [`Line.subpoints`](#link) but includes the end points.

parameters.name: line
parameters.comment: a Group or an Iterable<Pt> representing a line

signatures.comment: Create a set of random points inside a bounday.

parameters.name: count
parameters.comment: number of random points to create

parameters.name: dimensions
parameters.comment: number of dimensions in each point

signatures.comment:
Create a [`Flock`](#link) of [`Boid`](#link) agents that simulate flocking (also known as "boids"),
where each agent steers by three local rules: separation, alignment, and cohesion.
Advance the simulation by calling [`Flock.step`](#link) with the elapsed time.
See a [flocking demo here](https://ptsjs.org/demo/?name=create.flock).

Each agent starts with a random heading, drawn from [`Num.random`](#link), so seeding with
[`Num.seed`](#link) makes a flock reproducible.
signatures.returns_comment: an instance of the Flock class, which is a Group of Boids

parameters.name: pts
parameters.comment: a Group or an Iterable<Pt> of starting positions

signatures.comment: Create a grid of cells inside a boundary, where each cell is defined by a group of 2 Pt.
signatures.returns_comment: an array of Groups, where each group represents a rectangular cell

signatures.comment: Create an evenly distributed set of points (like a grid of points) inside a boundary.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.comment: a Pt or number array to specify where the point should be inside a cell. Default is [0.5, 0.5] which places the point in the middle.

signatures.comment: Given a group of Pts, return a new group of `Noise` Pts.

parameters.name: pts
parameters.comment: a Group or an Iterable<Pt>, in row-major order when treated as a grid

parameters.name: dx
parameters.comment: small increment value in x dimension

parameters.name: dy
parameters.comment: small increment value in y dimension

parameters.name: rows
parameters.comment: Optional row count to generate 2D noise

parameters.name: columns
parameters.comment: Optional column count (points per row) to generate 2D noise. When provided, each point's noise offset is (dx·column, dy·row) with row = floor(i/columns); when only `rows` is provided it is used as the points-per-row divisor instead.

signatures.comment: Create a set of Pts around a circular path.

Create a set of Pts that are randomly placed but never closer than `radius` to each other,
using Poisson-disk sampling (also called blue noise).
Compared with [`Create.distributeRandom`](#link), the points avoid clumping.
Sampling uses a finite candidate budget, so gaps can remain when it finishes.
The returned [`PoissonDisk`](#link) is a complete Group; to grow a set gradually instead,
construct a `PoissonDisk` and call its [`PoissonDisk.step`](#link) or [`PoissonDisk.sample`](#link).
See a [demo here](https://ptsjs.org/demo/?name=create.sampling).

Randomness comes from [`Num.random`](#link), so seeding with [`Num.seed`](#link) makes the set reproducible.
signatures.returns_comment: an instance of the PoissonDisk class, which is a Group of Pts

parameters.name: radius
parameters.comment: minimum distance between any two points
